evals.prompt: I defined a schedules.task with a cron and deployed it to production on our self-hosted Trigger.dev server. How do I attach the schedule to the production environment? Is there a schedules:attach command?
evals.expected_output: No attach step: the declarative cron syncs on dev and deploy; the CLI has no such command; limit environments with the environments option
expectations: States that a declarative schedule (cron on schedules.task) is synced by dev and deploy and needs no attach step
States that the CLI has no schedules:attach command
Mentions the environments option of the cron object to limit where it fires, and that without it every environment fires it
Explains that in staging and production only the task in the current deployment fires, and in dev only while the dev CLI runs

evals.prompt: My daily cron '0 9 * * *' on a self-hosted 4.7 server starts around 09:20, not 09:00. Why, and how do I make it start on time?
evals.expected_output: Server 4.6.0+ spreads new schedules over a window; set window to 0m; payload.timestamp is the nominal time
expectations: Explains that since server 4.6.0 new schedules are spread over a window after the cron time
Sets window: "0m" (or "0%") on the cron object for an exact start
Notes that payload.timestamp and upcoming show the nominal cron time, not the assigned start
Describes the window formats (whole minutes or hours up to 24h, or a percentage)

evals.prompt: Each user of my app should get a weekly report at the hour and timezone they choose, created from a Server Action. How do I create, pause and remove those schedules without duplicates?
evals.expected_output: A schedules.task without cron, schedules.create with externalId, deduplicationKey and timezone, deactivate and del, key scoped per project
expectations: Defines the task with schedules.task and no cron, reading payload.externalId in run
Calls schedules.create with task, cron, timezone, externalId and a required deduplicationKey built from the user
Uses schedules.deactivate to pause, schedules.activate to resume and schedules.del to remove, keeping the schedule id next to the user
Warns that the deduplicationKey is scoped to the project, not the environment
Treats externalId as an untrusted lookup key and validates the user in the run
